big_idea: CONGRUENT shapes are EXACTLY the same — same sides, same angles. We MATCH to test.
learning_intention: We are learning to identify congruent shapes.
success_criteria: I can MATCH 2 shapes by overlap.
I can name them CONGRUENT or NOT.
I can compare sides and angles.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Symmy and Flippy — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Symmy: I have TWO triangles. Are they CONGRUENT? Let's MATCH them — sit one ON TOP. If they fit perfectly, YES! Symmy opens: 'Same SIDE, same ANGLE — CONGRUENT!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Symmy and Flippy puppets. 'Friends — yesterday compose/decompose. Today CONGRUENT shapes.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write CONGRUENT on chart. 'Congruent = EXACTLY the same. Same sides. Same angles. Same shape.'

Demonstrate. Hold up 2 cut-out triangles. Place one ON TOP of the other. 'Match? YES. They're CONGRUENT.'

Non-example. 2 different-sized triangles. 'Sit one on top. DOESN'T match. NOT congruent.'

More examples:
- 2 squares of same size: CONGRUENT.
- 2 squares of different size: NOT congruent.
- 2 rectangles different orientation, same dims: CONGRUENT (rotation OK).
- 2 hexagons same size: CONGRUENT.
- A triangle and a square: NOT congruent (different shape).
- A rotated shape vs the same shape: CONGRUENT.

'Symmy says — to test, MATCH them. Place one on top. Do they fit? CONGRUENT. Doesn't fit? NOT.'

'Today we MATCH 16 cards into 8 congruent pairs.'

steps.instruction: Three stations. A: Match 16 cards into 8 pairs. B: Sort: congruent or not (10 pairs). C: Find a congruent partner for an unknown shape.
Stretch at C: include rotated shapes.

steps.teacher_prompt: Show: rotated square = still square; bigger square ≠ congruent.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two children test congruence three ways — (a) eyeball, (b) overlap, (c) measure sides. Class debates which is most reliable. Cite van Hiele (1986) Level 1 → Level 2 transition: from appearance to property-based reasoning.
steps.teacher_prompt: Symmy: 'Eyes can fool. Overlap and measure tell the truth.'

differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Sentence frame: 'These shapes ___ congruent because ___.' (are/are not)
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children pair up by clothing colour to demonstrate 'matching' concept. NO-MATERIALS PATH: teacher draws pairs of shapes on the board; child uses fingers to 'pick up' one shape and 'lay on' the other to test congruence visually.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: matches by overlap; names congruent; tests sides and angles.

consolidation.exit_routine: Symmy's congruence refrain — 'SIT one on TOP — does it MATCH? Same SIDE, same ANGLE — CONGRUENT!' Class chants 3x. Each child tests one shape pair.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says ROTATED shapes are NOT congruent — repairing the rotation-not-allowed trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On congruence, the trap is van Hiele Level 1 fixation (van Hiele 1986; Battista 2007): children judge shapes by appearance, not properties — they reject a rotated congruent shape as 'different.' Without rotation/reflection invariance, congruence work cannot ground.

Yesterday's area conservation primed the framing. Today: congruent = same SHAPE + same SIZE, regardless of orientation. Lesson 4 maps; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair at B. Two squares: one normal orientation, one rotated 45° (looks like a diamond). Same size. Child says NOT congruent.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Both squares are SAME SIZE. Symmy asks — what if you ROTATE one? Try sitting one on top after turning.'

Guide. Take the 'diamond' and rotate back to square. 'Now SIT one on top.' Match.

Generlise. 'Symmy says — congruent allows ROTATION. Same shape, different angle = STILL congruent. Test by rotating before matching.'

If still confused: provide pre-rotated shapes for matching.

Long-term: every congruence test includes rotation.
expected_student_responses: (Stretched) Identifies congruent shapes regardless of orientation.
common_misconceptions: Rotation = different shape. (Repair: rotation preserves shape.)
Different orientation = not congruent. (Repair: orientation doesn't matter.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child rejects rotated congruent shape: drill 'rotation doesn't change SIZE or SHAPE'; rotate physical cutouts until child accepts.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child accepts rotation but won't accept reflection: introduce mirror flip — 'flip is also OK.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can name congruent but cannot test: drill the overlap method — 'pick up shape A, place on shape B; if edges match exactly = CONGRUENT.'

parts_outline.task: Match 5 pairs as congruent or NOT.
For 4 shapes, find the congruent partner from a row.
Draw a shape congruent to a given one.

expected_image_assets: 4 shapes + row of options for Part 2
